title: Filesystem namespace alias and reparse-point confinement tribunal
hypothesis: A pure structural path tribunal can reject synthetic namespace aliases and reparse-point escapes before filesystem access while preserving repository-relative publication paths and bounded resource ceilings.
null_or_failure: Case variants bypass a deny rule, a reserved device name passes, an alternate stream is mistaken for a normal file, a drive-relative path escapes, an 8.3 alias bypasses identity checks, a reparse target leaves the owned root, resource limits disappear, or local checks become exhaustive-security assurance.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Mutate case, device names, trailing dots and spaces, alternate streams, UNC and extended prefixes, drive-relative forms, parent traversal, 8.3 aliases, reparse metadata, depth, and byte ceilings; reject unsafe strings without creating links, changing security, or touching paths outside the owned lane.
rollback_or_recovery: Reject and quarantine the path plan, retain the vector, restore repository-relative canonical naming and strict ceilings, and require independent security review and real environment testing before any broader assurance claim.
boundary: Synthetic namespace vectors do not establish exhaustive host security, independent security review, or production assurance.
